title: feat(types,react): TypeScript authoring types for the spec's public blocks, two spec-row blocks and page documents, by reference; SchemaRenderer's schema prop accepts them (objectui#11364)
body:
Refs #11364

Clause-②: yes
Why yes: new published TS types are added to `@object-ui/types`, and `@object-ui/react`'s `SchemaRendererProps.schema` accepts them, so the published TS surface widens.

Parent: objectui#8347. This is its preparation; the `BaseSchema` index-signature removal itself is not in this PR, and nothing here edits `BaseSchema`. The `props` alias question stays open for the maintainer (see "Open questions"), which is why this PR refers to the card rather than closing it.

Dispatched run, session `https://claude.ai/code/session_01VhxTqosz7wn54ahqyxgERT`. Draft, left for the seat.

## What changes

- **`@object-ui/types`**: `packages/types/src/authoring-nodes.ts`, exported from the main entry. Each type is derived by reference; no member is restated.
  - `PublicBlockNode`: one member per arm of `PublicBlockComponentSchema` (27 arms), each the arm's own `z.input` read off its SHAPE with the object config closed. `PublicBlockNodeOf` picks one member by its `type` literal (for example `'element:text'`).
  - `ElementTextInputNode` and `ElementRecordPickerNode`: no zod arm exists for these two, so each is built the way an arm is built: the zod `BaseSchema` shape extended with the `type` literal, the node envelope (`NODE_ENVELOPE`: `responsiveStyles`, the spec's `ResponsiveStylesSchema`), `properties` as the spec's `ComponentPropsMap` row, and the `body` / `children` tombstones every arm carries, each by reference. (Round 2: the round-1 type left out the envelope and the tombstones; see below.) The record picker also declares the node-level `dataSource` (the spec's `ElementDataSourceSchema`) its renderer reads, and leaves the bag's `object` optional for the spec props gate's `dataSource` waiver, the same waiver the `element:number` arm mirrors.
  - `PageDocumentNode`: the spec's `PageSchema` input with `type` (the page kind) required, the document `PageView` hands to `SchemaRenderer` (objectui#9642).
  - `AuthoringNode`: their union.
- **`@object-ui/react`**: `SchemaRendererProps.schema` is now `BaseSchema | AuthoringNode | string | null | undefined`. No index signature and no `Record` on the prop. `toRenderableSchema` returns `SchemaRendererProps['schema']` by reference, so the bridge's return type widens with the prop in this release (the `.d.ts` text of `schema-input` does not change, so the H5 diff cannot show it).
- **4 component test files**: the three `page:tabs` literals move `items` into `properties` (where `PageTabsProps` declares it); the `action:button` literals move `label` / `actionType` into the bag (objectui#11183's landed shape) and the helper takes the arm's node type beside `BaseSchema`; the `element:text_input` literal handed to `renderComponent` is typed as `ElementTextInputNode`. CASE A in `action-params-templates-7867` keeps its node-level `params` object: that spelling is what it proves is not read (objectui#10289). `SchemaRenderer` hoists the bag onto the node, so every renderer reads the same values; the suites below are green.
- **Pins**: `packages/types/src/__tests__/authoring-nodes-11364.test.ts` (new) and assertion 1 of `packages/react/src/__tests__/SchemaRenderer.propsResolution.test.ts` (the prop's exact union).
- **Docs**: `packages/types/README.md`, `packages/react/README.md`, `content/docs/guide/schema-rendering.md`.
- **Changesets**: `.changeset/11364-public-block-ts-faces.md` (types minor, react minor). Three pending entries this release makes false get a dated, append-only note, each with its frontmatter byte-identical (md5 of the frontmatter lines unchanged): `9256-public-blocks-content-channels.md` ("This package has no TypeScript declaration of these nodes"), `8908-bridge-falsy-primitives.md` ("The return type is unchanged", round 2) and `schema-input-bridge-permanent-4622.md` (the prop's union spelled as it was, round 2).

## The pin

`authoring-nodes-11364.test.ts` runs in every `type-check` today, before objectui#8347 lands. It builds `PostRemovalSchema`: the prop's union with `BaseSchema`'s index signatures stripped at the type level. Against it:

- `{ type: 'element:text', properties: { content: 'Hello' } }` compiles;
- `properties: { contnet: 'Hello' }` is refused, as is a node-level `contnet` and a `properties` bag on a `button` node.

It also checks that no arm is lost by the derivation (`PublicBlockNode['type']` equals the union's own), and that no member carries an index signature. A control proves that check can fire: the bare `z.input` of the same arms does carry one. Every `@ts-expect-error` there is consumed (an unused one is TS2578).

## Round 2 (contract record `5933841900`, FAIL on `29acb0107`)

Head `6af8e9da3`. `origin/main` was merged again (`3ae919307`, no conflicts, no rebase).

- **A, the spec-row nodes.** `SpecRowNode` is now the type-level twin of an arm's `BaseSchema.extend(...)`: `Omit` of the zod `BaseSchema` shape by the own keys, then the `type` literal, `typeof NODE_ENVELOPE`, `properties`, and `body` / `children` as `retirementTombstone`'s return type, all type-only imports. The spec's own `PageComponentSchema` refuses a node-level `children` on `element:text_input` and `element:record_picker` (`unrecognized_keys`), as it does on `element:text`. Measured three ways:
  - before the fix (type-level P1 simulation): through the union, `responsiveStyles` compiled on `element:text` and was TS2353 on both spec-row nodes, and a node-level `children` was refused on `element:text` but compiled on `element:text_input`; on the node types, both spec-row nodes accepted `children` and refused `responsiveStyles`;
  - after the fix, under the REAL P1 mutation, through the actual `SchemaRenderer` `schema` prop (a throwaway probe compiled against the built `react` dist and the mutated `types` dist): `responsiveStyles` compiles on `element:text`, `element:text_input` and `element:record_picker`, and a node-level `children` is refused (TS2353) on all three, exactly as on `element:text`. The census still reads 10, and the restore is proven;
  - the pin's reverse check: with the fix ablated through `ablation-replace.mjs` (restore to `HEAD` proven), the new pin case turns red as predicted: TS2353 on the two styled spec-row literals and TS2578 on the three spec-row `children` directives, with the `element:text` control unchanged.
- **B, the bridge.** The `11364` entry now says the bridge's return widens with the prop; `8908` gets the dated note. `schema-input-bridge-permanent-4622.md` spells the prop's old union too, so it gets the same note by the same rule.
- **C.** The `11364` entry no longer says nothing stops compiling "because `BaseSchema` still carries its index signature". It says every value the old union accepted is still accepted, that a key absent from a closed member is TS2339 on a union whatever the signature allows, and that no caller here reads a key off the prop's type or the bridge's return (the `Type Check` job re-derives that).
- **Round-2 gates** (at `7638daa9e`; `6af8e9da3` adds only a changeset `.md`): `@object-ui/components^...` closure build exit 0; `type-check` types / react / components exit 0, 0 errors, scripts echoed; the pin and `SchemaRenderer.propsResolution` under vitest 2 files, 8 tests passed; `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations`, `check:spec-symbols`, `check:phantom-deps`, `check:unreferenced-sources` all exit 0 (re-run at `6af8e9da3`). P1 census 10, src 0.

## Measurements (round 1, at `29acb0107` unless noted)

**H1, the population** (objectui#8347's P1 mutation, `BaseSchema`'s `[key: string]: any` deleted alone through `ablation-replace.mjs`, types rebuilt each leg, `@object-ui/components`' test program):

| head | test-program errors | src-program errors |
|---|--:|--:|
| `b5b0afea5` (base) | 30 | 0 |
| `29acb0107` (this PR) | 10 | 0 |

The 30 at base, by reading each site: 13 public blocks (3 `element:text`, 7 `element:text_input`, 3 `element:record_picker`), 3 `page:tabs`, 5 `action:button`, 2 page documents (`type: 'home'`), 4 `props` alias, 1 `content` probe, 2 test-registered probe type. The card's "14" public blocks reads 13 here; the 30 includes the `content` probe.

The 10 left at head, each a literal no referenced type can or should accept:

- 4 `props` alias (`alias-precedence-cross-channel`): waiting on the `props` question.
- 1 `content` on `label` (`form-renderers`): the retired-spelling probe.
- 2 `properties: 'not-a-bag'` on a test-registered probe type (`degenerate-config-bag`).
- 1 node-level `params` object on `action:button` CASE A: the objectui#10289 probe.
- 2 `visibility` on `element:text` (`page-variables`): the spec's deprecated alias, which objectui#10872 kept off the TS face; `SchemaRenderer` reads it only defensively for raw metadata. TS2353 hid this second key behind `properties` at base.

All 10 compile today; they are objectui#8347's flips. Every leg's restore is proven: `ok restored: blob == HEAD (ce2bc9e31dc6) and git diff HEAD is empty`, dist index-signature count back to 2. The mutation is never committed.

**H2, arm or row per block.**

| node | zod arm | spec row | type here |
|---|---|---|---|
| `element:text`, `page:tabs`, `action:button`, and the other 24 public blocks | yes | yes | `PublicBlockNode` member |
| `element:text_input` | none (the validator refuses it at `type`) | `ElementTextInputPropsSchema` | `ElementTextInputNode` |
| `element:record_picker` | none (refused at `type`) | `ElementRecordPickerPropsSchema` | `ElementRecordPickerNode` |
| page kind (`home`, `app`, `record`, `utility`) | none (`PageNodeSchema` is `type: 'page'`; refused at `type`) | `PageSchema` | `PageDocumentNode` |

The PM's prediction (a one-line `z.input` of each arm) is falsified in one respect: the zod `BaseSchema` is `.passthrough()`, so the bare `z.input` of an arm has `keyof` = `string` (`[k: string]: unknown`), which would put the removed index signature back. The derivation reads the arm's shape with the config closed instead. The spec rows of `element:image`, `element:metadata_viewer`, `element:filter` and `element:form` are not typed here: none appears in the census.

**H3, the prop.** Under P1, `SpecPageComponent` is refused by exactly one shared key: `visibleWhen` (`BaseSchema` says `string`, the spec says `string` or an Expression envelope). Its other keys are spec-only and do not block a non-fresh value. So no union of referenced types makes it assignable while keeping the pin:

- adding the spec's `PageComponent` to the union makes it assignable, but `properties: { contnet }` on `element:text` then compiles (measured);
- widening `BaseSchema.visibleWhen` to `ExpressionWire` (type-level simulation) makes it assignable AND keeps the misspelling refused, but that edits `BaseSchema`, which is excluded here.

That is the fork the dispatch asked to be reported, and it is in "Open questions". Each new node type IS assignable to the prop, and the union is pinned exactly.

**H4, the spec's page row.** `PageSchema.type` is `PageTypeSchema` (`record`, `app`, `home`, `list`, `utility`; default `record`); `kind` is the override mode (`full`, `slotted`, `html`, `react`, `jsx`). `page:tabs` `items` is a member of the bag (`PageTabsProps`), not of the node; each item requires `label` and `children`.

**H5, the published surface** (base `b5b0afea5` built in a comparison worktree, against this branch):

- `@object-ui/types` `dist`: one new file, `authoring-nodes.d.ts` (references only: `z.input` of the arms and spec rows), and one new `export type` line in `index.d.ts`. 13 `zod/*.zod.d.ts` files differ only by the print order of inferred members; each has a token multiset equal to base's (whitespace, the union bar and trailing punctuation normalised).
- `@object-ui/react` `dist`: `SchemaRenderer.d.ts` gains the `AuthoringNode` import and the widened prop, and an existing inferred `render()` return type prints its union members in a different order.

## Open questions (in the report, with the four-axis frame)

1. **The `props` alias on the TS authoring face.** Measured producers: objectui's 1720 non-test TS/TSX files author no node `props` (control `properties: {` reads 28); tracked JSON has 0 `"props": {` files (control 10); objectstack `examples/**` TS at local `95fed33a2` has 0 (control 52); the published skill teaches node-level `props` as WRONG. The only authors are the 4 `alias-precedence` probes. Undecided here, per the dispatch.
2. **`SpecPageComponent` assignability** (H3): widen `BaseSchema.visibleWhen` to the spec's union (objectui#8347's file), or add `PageComponent` to the prop and lose the bag check, or leave it unassignable.

## Acceptance notes

- In the prop's union `BaseSchema` (`type: string`) still accepts any node structurally, so these types judge each node's own keys and values (bag members, `kind`, `items`) but do not make a member's required keys required. A page document without `label` still compiles against the prop. Requiredness stays the validator's.
- `SchemaNode` is not widened. Measured: with the signature present, a reader of a widened `SchemaNode` that reads an undeclared key (`columns`) turns TS2339 on the closed member, where today it compiles through the index signature. A literal nested in a `children` slot therefore still needs its own typing after objectui#8347.
- The TS face now types three node kinds that `AnyComponentSchema` still refuses at `type` (`element:text_input`, `element:record_picker`, page documents). That refusal is the population `registered-types-validate-ratchet-10859` counts, not a judgement that the nodes are invalid.
- Finding, not carded: the spec's `PageComponentSchema` normalises `visibleWhen` into a `{ dialect: 'cel', source }` envelope at parse, the renderer evaluates it, and `AnyComponentSchema` refuses the envelope (`invalid_type` at `visibleWhen`). Measured through the built validator. Same root as open question 2.
- Not carded: AGENTS.md #4 still teaches the flat `action:button` executor spelling that objectui#11183 moved into the bag. That file is governed; objectui#11183's lane carries it.
